evals.name: fix-hairball-flowchart
evals.prompt:
This diagram in my ADR (doc/adr/0007-service-layers.md) is an unreadable mess — every service points at the shared core and it's just a tangle of crossing arrows. Clean it up so a reader can actually parse it. Here's the current block:

```mermaid
graph TD
  auth["auth-service"]
  billing["billing-service"]
  notify["notify-service"]
  search["search-service"]
  reporting["reporting-service"]
  core["core-lib shared utilities, config, logging"]
  pg[("postgres")]
  auth --> core
  billing --> core
  notify --> core
  search --> core
  reporting --> core
  auth --> pg
  billing --> pg
  reporting --> pg
  billing -.-> auth
```

Write the improved markdown to doc/adr/0007-service-layers.md.
evals.expected_output: A markdown file with a cleaner mermaid diagram: the five identical service-->core edges collapsed via a subgraph + single group edge, services grouped, postgres kept as a datastore, the billing-.->auth dependency preserved as a distinct edge, plus a prose 'reading the diagram' legend.

evals.name: architecture-from-description
evals.prompt: I'm writing the README for our notification service. Add a diagram showing how the pieces fit together. The service has an HTTP API and a background worker; they share a Postgres database and a Redis queue. The worker calls two external providers, Twilio (SMS) and SendGrid (email). The API is called by our main web app. Put the diagram in README.md under a new '## Architecture' section.
evals.expected_output: README.md with an Architecture section containing a mermaid diagram that groups internal components vs external providers, uses a datastore shape for Postgres/Redis, distinguishes internal services from external systems, labels the relationships, and is followed by a short legend.

evals.name: sequence-oauth-flow
evals.prompt: Document the Google OAuth login flow in docs/auth.md. The flow: the browser hits our app's /login, the app redirects the browser to Google's consent screen, the user approves, Google redirects back to our /callback with a code, our app exchanges the code with Google for an access token, then creates a session and redirects the browser to the dashboard. Add a diagram and a couple sentences explaining it.
evals.expected_output: docs/auth.md with a mermaid SEQUENCE diagram (not a flowchart) showing browser, app, and Google as participants with ordered request/response messages, autonumbered, plus a short prose explanation.
